mainEntity.name: How does the arid Verde Valley climate affect drywall drying and texture application?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dry climates across Cottonwood and Camp Verde speed up surface evaporation, which can cause drywall mud to dry out along its edges before it properly cures. When compound dries too rapidly in arid, windy, or warm environments, it can develop hairline shrinkage cracks, edge curling on paper tape, and chalky adhesion failures. Contractors manage this by using chemical-setting compounds (hot mud) rather than standard air-drying compounds for base coats, mixing mud in smaller batches, and controlling cross-drafts inside the home during the texturing and drying stages.
acceptedAnswer.description: Dry desert air can cause drywall mud to dry prematurely, leading to shrinkage and weak bonds. Using setting compounds and controlling ventilation ensures proper curing.
